A gem in Saigon
Nov 2025 • Friends
A true gem in Saigon - Mustard Indian restaurant and Bistro

Our experience at Mustard Indian restaurant and Bistro was absolutely wonderful. From the moment we arrived, we were greeted with such warmth and genuine hospitality by Bishal and his brother Purshottam - they truly make every guest feel like family. Chef Dinesh deserves a special praise for his exceptional cooking ; every dish was perfectly spiced , full of authentic flavours, and so much like home. 
The food was so good that we simply couldn’t resist going back for a second time ! A special thanks for the complimentary dessert on both the days . Mustard Indian restaurant is a must visit in Saigon for anyone craving real Indian food served with heartfelt warmth and care. Special thanks to the entire team for the lime sugar and salt🙏

Pure and entertaining flavors
Jul 2025 • Friends
The food is prepared with such care that the flavor is impeccable while completely pure without artificiality. The menu provides a wide array of vegetarian dishes from starters to main courses including biryani, tandoori and momos, fresh juices and lassis. For vegetarians there are options from every type of dish.

The restaurant was full which is no wonder, as the whole team displayed a distinguished skill. The overall vibe of Mustard the Indian restaurant is fine, clean and inviting. 

We visited as a travel couple/group. We enjoyed super friendly approach by the manager, who speaks an astonishing amount of languages - English, Nepalese, Hindi and Vietnamese among others. Thank you for the hospitality which truly made our night.

Amazingly good
Nov 2024 • Couples
As promised, a review of our dinner tonight - Indian cuisine.

After a chat with a Wink Hotels local guide, we were recommended to try Mustard The Indian Restaurant.

A quick 'grab' ride and then a short walk down one of the fabulous side alleys to the restaurant, and we settled in.

We started with paneer pakora, and mains was butter chicken, a paneer butter korma, steamed rice, a huge garlic butter naan and raita - well let me tell you - this would have to be the nicest, flavoursome Indian we have ever had OMG everything was amazing.

We ate dinner traditionally (tried to) with our hands and naan with forks assisting from time to time, at the end of the meal - finger bowls were presented to clean with.

The last surprise was a spoonful of fennel seeds, along with candy mixed it to aid in digestion (is what we were told)

Have attached photos here of the food we had (and we were full as). Everything totalled was $38.55 aud!!

If you get to Ho Chi Minh City, make sure you visit these guys .
